v.why: Replacing none with conv3x3 on the edge into the output adds a whole learnable path, which gains more than swapping one parametric op for another.
Replacing conv3x3 with conv1x1 loses receptive field and capacity, whereas replacing pool or none with conv1x1 is a gain, so the edit is worse when it replaces conv3x3.
An identity shortcut on the direct edge already eases optimization, so a deep conv on edge 5 is partly redundant and adds less.
A conv feeding node 2 gives edge 5 meaningful features to transform, so stacked convs add more than when node 2 carries nothing useful.
With edge 1 removed, node 2 receives little useful input and a conv on edge 5 has less to process.
A conv on edge 0 builds features at node 1 that edge 4 can refine into a deeper path to the output.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 is disconnected and a conv on edge 4 has no input, so the edit does nothing.
Adding the direct identity path where none existed improves gradient flow and gains more than replacing a conv or pool, which are already informative.
Pooling after a conv smooths already-learned features and is less harmful than pooling raw input, which discards information.
Replacing the identity shortcut with pooling blurs the direct path and removes the easiest route for signal, which hurts more than replacing none.
